title: private-deploy-networking-incident-notes
content:
Summary:
- Notes for debugging customer private deployment connectivity issues (VPC peering + DNS + egress).
- Symptoms: control-plane components in customer VPC cannot reach Redwood Private control-plane endpoints intermittently; TLS handshake fails sometimes; DNS resolution returns NXDOMAIN in some pods.

Timeline / Context:
- 2026-02-18 09:12 PST: Customer reported failures for onboarding job (canary) — logs show connect errors to control-plane (redwood-private.example.com).
- 2026-02-18 09:25 PST: Repro confirmed from bastion in customer VPC: curl to endpoint sometimes times out, sometimes TLS 403/handshake errors.
- Customer network: VPC peering to our infra, route tables mirrored via peering (no transit gateway). Egress is via NAT GW in private subnet.

Commands / Outputs I tried (raw):
1) dig against customer pod resolver:
$ kubectl exec -it onboarding-0 -- dig +short redwood-private.example.com
10.10.34.22
# sometimes returns empty / NXDOMAIN

2) curl with verbose showing TLS handshake issues:
$ curl -v https://redwood-private.example.com/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://redwood-private.example.com/health
*   Trying 10.10.34.22:443...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to redwood-private.example.com (10.10.34.22) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* <-- TLS handshake completed -->
* SSL certificate problem: self signed certificate in certificate chain
* Closing connection 0

Observation: client sees a cert that looks wrong (self-signed) only on some requests — indicates we might be hitting a wrong backend (internal test instance) due to routing asymmetry/load balancer.

3) traceroute from bastion (shows large jump / MTU not likely but routing asymmetry visible):
$ traceroute 10.10.34.22
1 10.0.0.1 0.5 ms
2 192.168.8.14 1.2 ms
3 172.16.254.3 12.1 ms
4 10.200.200.2 45.6 ms
5 10.10.34.22 46.0 ms

No clear loops but hop 4 is our peering router cluster where we saw error spikes.

4) tcpdump on customer-to-peering interface (short capture):
$ sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.10.34.22 and port 443 -w /tmp/cap.pcap
# Observation: SYN / SYN-ACK completes, then immediate RST from remote on ~1/10 requests. No ICMP fragmentation.

5) openssl s_client to inspect cert chain and SNI:
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.10.34.22:443 -servername redwood-private.example.com
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN=internal-test-01
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
No peer certificate available (weird, intermittent)

Guess: requests are sometimes routed to an internal test node that serves a different cert (internal-test-01) — likely stale instance still in routing table or LB pool.

DNS oddities:
- Kubernetes cluster uses split-horizon resolver (CoreDNS) that forwards unknown hostnames to customer VPC resolver. Some pods return NXDOMAIN for redwood-private.example.com for ~1/20 queries.
- Hypothesis: DNS TTL / cache poisoning? Or conditional forwarders failing over to default resolver intermittently.

Commands for DNS debug:
$ kubectl exec -it coredns-0 -- cat /etc/resolv.conf# shows forwarders to 10.0.0.2 (customer resolver)
$ dig @10.0.0.2 redwood-private.example.com +tcp +trace; sometimes returns the AAAA/ A, sometimes fails to reach authoritative.

Egress / NAT checks:
- Confirmed NAT gateway metrics: spikes in connections ~09:20–09:40 correlating with errors.
- NAT logs show source translations for some flows rewriting to unexpected IPs (NAT port exhaustion around peak?).
- Hypothesis: NAT port reuse leading to session collisions causing TLS sessions to be picked up by unrelated backend connection stateful firewall at peering side.

Security groups / ACLs:
- Verified customer SG rules allow outbound 443 to our peering CIDR. Ingress rules on our peering side allow ephemeral ports back. No obvious drop.

Other commands run (quick list):
- iptables -L -n on affected host 
- netstat -tn | grep 10.10.34.22
- curl --resolve redwood-private.example.com:443:10.10.34.22 https://redwood-private.example.com/health 
- ssh to internal-test-01 (found in cert CN) -> instance is decommissioned but still in inventory; instance IP belongs to a legacy LB pool.

Findings so far:
- There appears to be two problems compounding:
  1) Intermittent routing to a legacy internal test backend that serves a wrong cert. Likely stale target in LB or peering routing table (BGP?) on our side.
  2) Intermittent DNS resolution failures for some pods due to split-horizon forwarding flapping to a resolver that sometimes cannot answer (possibly rate-limited or flapping connection to customer's resolver).
- NAT gateway port churn likely exacerbating session reuse and intermittent resets but not root cause of wrong cert.

Immediate next steps / to-dos:
- [ ] Confirm LB pool membership: check control-plane LB target group for stale internal-test instance IPs / deregister if present (eng-infra to check). Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/912
- [ ] Ask customer to run continuous dig from their resolver (script) and capture failure windows (helpful to correlate).
- [ ] Increase DNS logging on CoreDNS for conditional forwarder queries for redwood-private.example.com (add log plugin for 24h).
- [ ] Rotate cert for control-plane as a short-term mitigation to avoid serving wrong CN but beware this masks underlying routing issue.
- [ ] Check NAT GW CloudWatch for port exhaustion metrics and scale NAT or add EIP pool if needed.
- [ ] Validate peering route tables and any stale BGP sessions (network team).

Notes / hypotheses to keep iterating:
- Could be asymmetric routing where some traffic from customer hits a different egress device that NATs to a different public IP, which our peering LPG matches to legacy backend.
- Also consider MTU issues if large TLS handshake with SNI extension fragments — unlikely based on tcpdump.

Useful artifacts / places to check quickly:
- infra LB target group: infra/load-balancers/target-groups/control-plane-targets
- jira: INC-3421 (primary incident) and NET-789 (peering changes last month)
- slack: #private-deployments and thread slack://C9AB2CD34/thread-incident-3421

Rough log snippets copied from customer (sanitized):
[2026-02-18T09:22:14Z] onboarding-job: ERROR connect redwood-private.example.com:443: TLS handshake error: certificate verify failed: self signed certificate in chain
[2026-02-18T09:23:02Z] kube-dns: NXDOMAIN for redwood-private.example.com from 10.0.0.2

If no progress in 24h escalate to eng-networking (paging) and open postmortem draft (template: confluence://incident-postmortem-template).

Personal notes: keep conversation to technical channels only for now; customer is sensitive to security implications of 'internal-test' backend mention. Coordinate with customer success before public comms.

-- Olivia
(last edited 2026-02-28)
